correctness.rationale: The two-sided marked-Poisson stochastic integral exists with all finite moments under |Q|<=c<1, and synchronous contraction yields invariant-law uniqueness. The absolute-value process is reflected Brownian motion with jump kernel |Q|R, so its entire stationary path law depends only on the law of |Q|. A stationary one-time position is a centered Gaussian mixture with conditional variance determined by Q², hence cannot reveal reset signs either. For X_t=Z_t x+U_t, the leading coefficient of P_n(t,x)=E(X_t^n|X_0=x) is E Z_t^n=exp[-r(1-m_n)t]. As m_n→0, lambda_n→r; the rates recover all multiplier power moments and compact moment determinacy recovers the signed law. For at most m atoms and known r, moments 0 through 2m-1 solve a Vandermonde system. Lx=−r(1−q)x and Lx²=2D−r(1−q²)x² give the two covariance rates and q=lambda2/lambda1−1, r=lambda1/(1−q), D=V lambda2/2. Independent exact substitution at q=±2/3, r=5/4, D=3/7 confirmed same variance 216/175, squared rate 25/36 and differing signed rates 5/12,25/12. The 211 saved check.py assertions only corroborate algebra, not reflected path equality.
